messages:
maya: Heads-up — during the EU canary yesterday we saw a weird inspect token reuse across tenants when requests got routed to the fallback region. Not a breach but definitely an exposure path if left unchecked.
aj: ugh. do we have a repro? logs/trace id?
maya: trace: `req/0a9c-eu->fallback/1b2d`. I can paste stack if needed. The flow: tenant A -> EU -> short outage -> routed to NA -> console inspect token still valid for tenant B's request id (same token format), console allowed preview for a few seconds.
sam: that's bad. sounds like our inspect token scoping isn't strict enough (region/route/tenant). currently token is just `inspect:<hmac>` with ttl.
katrina: yup — current token binder: hmac(request_id || user_id || issued_at). Missing route/region and also missing `tenant_id` in some legacy routes.
aj: proposal: bind token to (tenant_id, route_id, region, request_id) + timestamp, sign with per-region key and enforce TTL at the edge. If mismatch, drop to redacted preview automatically.
maya: ^ agree. add to that: token should be single-use or single-request. We saw a race where a replay during failover was accepted.
sam: single-use is correct for safety but ops will whine about needing re-inspect for legitimate retries. UX tradeoff.
maya: UX idea: allow a short re-inspect window (e.g., 15s) for the same request_id but only from the same console session, otherwise single-use.
aj: implement via nonce store keyed by token-hash + session-id + small TTL. cheap in redis.
katrina: routing-wise, we should also have the router attach a `route_fingerprint` header before handing to runtime. Token signer includes that fingerprint. If router changes (failover), fingerprint won't match -> runtime rejects.
sam: console changes: show a tiny banner when inspect fails due to scope mismatch: "Inspect token invalid for this region/route — request was served from fallback. Request redacted for safety. Request new inspect?" One-click re-request would generate a new token after audit check.
maya: we need an audit flow: every re-inspect must capture reason + approver (or console will auto-approve if requester is owner and within 1m). Otherwise escalate to oncall.
aj: implementation sketch (pseudo):
```
# token payload
{
  "tid": "tenant_123",
  "rid": "route_abcd",
  "rfinger": "rf_789",
  "req": "0a9c",
  "exp": 1700000000,
  "reuse": 0
}
# sign with region key
```
edge: verify sig, check exp, check rfinger == X-Route-Fingerprint, check reuse==0 || (session==owner && within 15s)

katrina: also we should tie quota consumption to inspect requests separately. Inspecting full request/response should count against a small audit quota per-tenant (to limit scanning abuse). e.g., 10 inspect tokens / tenant / day by default.
sam: console UX should show quota left when you click inspect so users don't be surprised.
maya: ops alerting: if a tenant's inspect rate spikes, trigger a signal and temporarily suspend auto-approve re-inspects.
deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: feature/inspect-token-hardening -> canary to eng-staging at 2026-03-22T03:00Z :rocket:
aj: follow-ups: 1) add `route_fingerprint` emitter in router (katrina). 2) make token binder include tenant+route+region (maya). 3) console: show quota + one-click re-request with audit text (sam). 4) ops: define threshold and alert (ops oncall) (maya).
sam: I'll draft console copy for the banner + modal. keeping it short: "This request was served from a fallback region; for privacy we need to re-authorize an inspect. Provide reason (optional) and confirm." Add a link to audit log.
katrina: I'll add the router header and a small migration plan. edge behavior: if header missing, treat as unscoped and reject token (fail-safe). also add a graceful rollout: start rejecting for new routes only, then flip global.
maya: thanks. posting internal RFC in docs/ later. tagging @eng-oncall for threshold planning. :thumbsup:
aj: thanks all. filing follow-up tickets and a canary plan.
